title: Clockface slicing: responsive legend condensation and TTS-friendly time-series summaries
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: High-density time-series charts are producing verbose legends and long tooltips that bloat the DOM, increase reflow cost and produce unusable screen reader output for customers with large datasets. The goal is a design pattern that: 1) condenses legend content responsively across widths and densities, 2) provides a short TTS-friendly summary for screen readers with optional drill-down, and 3) reduces runtime paint/DOM overhead with a canvas-first fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Legend condenses to a compact stacked or overflow carousel pattern under 380px width without losing color mapping
Screen reader receives a single summarized aria-live message per focus event (max 160 chars) with a keyboard-accessible way to expand to full series details
Canvas fallback for dense series activated automatically above 50 series or 200k rendered points and meets interaction parity for hover/focus
Design tokens for legend spacing, token colors, and condensed typography created and documented in the design system
Implementation PR merged with unit/integration tests and perf benchmark comparison (<15% increase in first-paint vs baseline)
design_notes: Introduce 'clockface slicing' as an affordance in the condensed legend: instead of full timestamps, show relative sector markers (e.g., 12:00, 06:00) mapped to precomputed buckets to reduce label churn
The condensed legend should use a single-line color chip + abbreviated label (max 18 chars). On keyboard focus, aria-expanded toggles the full label and series summary region.
TTS summary: compute top-3 series by recent delta (last N points) server-side or in a lightweight client worker and render a one-line summary like 'Top changes: Orders +12%, Revenue -3%, CTR steady'

Performance trade-off: precompute bucket aggregates for clockface markers (client worker) to avoid expensive on-hover aggregations. Use requestAnimationFrame + passive pointer events for hover interactions.

Accessibility trade-offs: avoid sending full dataset to SR via DOM. Instead provide a generated summary and an 'expand' action that lazily hydrates full details into an offscreen region when requested.
decisions: Use canvas layer for primary series rendering and reserve DOM for interactive hit targets and condensed legend only
Adopt a worker-based aggregator for clockface bucket computation to keep main thread responsive
Expose two new design tokens: 'legend.condensedGap' and 'legend.clockfaceFontSize' with backward-compatible defaults
Keep tooltip previews as ephemeral canvas overlays that materialize a lightweight DOM card only on persistent focus (>300ms)
implementation_notes: Frontend: add LegendCondense component with strategies: shrink, overflow-carousel, clockface-buckets. Default strategy selection is based on measured containerWidth and seriesCount.
Worker: histogram-style bucketer keyed by timezone-normalized epoch slices to avoid label jitter when panning/zooming
Backend: optional precomputations endpoint for dashboards with large ingest to provide pre-bucketed summaries
QA: produce automated a11y checks using axe-core and manual screen reader pass (NVDA + VoiceOver) on condensed and expanded states
